alerts.source_line: Before asking how a circuit keeps a value, we need to know how its activity represents that value and what makes the activity variable. We begin with the spikes that cells send and the patterns of firing rates across a population. A model of spike counts then shows why one brief observation can be uncertain and how combining counts from several cells can help. We then learn how to tell whether measurements vary together and how to separate random spreading from a change in the average value. Those distinctions will let us interpret both a memory model and measurements of eye motion.

alerts.source_line: **Physical meaning: a shared command can survive averaging across neurons.** If a common input raises the firing of many motor neurons that pull the eye in the same direction, their effects add. Independent extra and missing spikes partly cancel when those neurons act together. The paper compares the measured eye displacement with a displacement predicted from one neuron's spikes, after converting both to degrees. That prediction is an analysis of a recording, not an extra command sent to the muscles. A relationship between the two is evidence to test against a model of shared input and private noise. It does not mean that the one recorded cell causes all the movement.

alerts.source_line: **Physical meaning: random wandering differs from a persistent directional error.** Let $x(t)$ be horizontal eye angle in degrees and let $\ell$ be the time between two measurements, called the lag, in seconds. [The [**displacement**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} $\Delta x=x(t+\ell)-x(t)$ is the change in that angle.]{.definition-explanation} A random change in the maintained command can move the eye left in one interval and right in another. The average displacement can then be close to zero while individual displacements are large. A persistent imbalance in the command can instead make the average displacement grow in one direction. Muscles smooth the command before it becomes eye movement, so the timescale of the observation also matters.

alerts.source_line: The independence assumption also has a precise scope. Newly generated spike-count fluctuations are conditionally independent given the present state. The paper discusses such correlated models as future extensions ([Discussion, p. 5, paragraph beginning “Our spiking model”](../papers/burak-fiete-2012-persistent-activity.pdf#page=5&zoom=125,0,142)).
